referee_caveats_inferred: Photosphere radius depends on assuming Tb = Teff = 3600 K and a uniform disk, and IRS 7 is only ~10 sigma at the beam size, so the R uncertainty of 60 Rsun looks small
The 34.5 GHz limit and the 340 GHz flux come from different epochs and a star variable in size, so the spectral index limit is loose
Te and ne rely on optically thin LTE, a spherical shell geometry, the assumed continuum spectral index 0.1 and He+/H+ = 0.09
Shell continuum at 232 GHz is scaled from 340 GHz rather than measured, and may include stellar photospheric flux
Mass loss rate comes from a single expansion time scale with Vexp derived from the line width; non-thermal broadening and the dominance of ambient gas are not excluded
Bow shock interpretation rests on a 2D proper motion plus line-of-sight velocity and a rough energy estimate

missing_for_reproduction: Execution block list and spectral window setup for both projects
Imaging parameters for the continuum clean (cell, image size, threshold, masks) and self-calibration settings
Exact flux extraction procedure for IRS 7 in the presence of Sgr A* sidelobes
Integration region and velocity range definitions used for the line integral and Gaussian fit
Error propagation for R, Te, ne
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Three 340 GHz execution blocks plus one DDT dataset, roughly tens of GB raw; the calibrated cubes needed here are a few GB
reproducibility.score_reason: Both project codes are printed and the formulae and results are numeric, but imaging, self-calibration and flux extraction details are missing and the details sit in an earlier paper.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public status of the data is not stated, and calibration, imaging and flux extraction settings are incomplete or deferred to earlier work.
